extraction.name: ArtifactsBench
extraction.description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifacts. It contains 1,825 executable queries across nine domains and uses automated multimodal evaluation with staged screenshots and checklist-guided judging to assess visual fidelity, interaction dynamics, and code quality.
extraction.creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
extraction.citeAs: Tencent Hunyuan Team. ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation. arXiv:2507.04952v2, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was constructed through a multi-stage pipeline that aggregated candidate tasks from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots, then filtered, de-duplicated, rewrote, calibrated, and validated them.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Candidate tasks were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Checklist generation & calibration: each query is paired with a 10-dimension checklist; they "LLM-draft and then human-refine for specificity and screenability," with a "10% manually curated seed" and "Cohen’s κ≥0.8 among annotators"; for validation, they ran a "double-blind study on 280 queries and 6 models, judged by multiple front-end engineers," where samples were randomized and "the final human ground-truth score represents the median of the individual annotators’ ratings."
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The "final human ground-truth score represents the median of the individual annotators’ ratings"; agreement between automated referee and humans is measured by pairwise consistency rate (Pair ACC), counting pairs where MLLM referee and human judges agree on rank ordering; the checklist seed calibration "achieves Cohen’s κ≥0.8 among annotators."
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Single-multimodal-referee evaluations can suffer from hallucination, prompt sensitivity, limited awareness of engineering/code quality, and version drift; minor discrepancies are observed in fine-grained scoring of certain complex interactive tasks, reflecting potential cognitive biases in how different MLLMs interpret long-horizon interaction logic and dynamic visual feedback.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: For highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions, the discrete sampling of screenshots at fixed intervals may not fully capture the fluidity, correctness, and robustness of the entire interactive experience; ArtifactsBench currently focuses on evaluating the quality of the final artifact generated in a single turn from a given prompt and does not assess an LLM’s capability to iteratively refine an artifact, debug its own code, or plan and execute a multi-step development process
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to provide the community with a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The query quality filtering aims to select high-quality, practical, complete, and privacy-free queries and avoid sensitive personal information such as phone numbers, addresses, or other identifiable details
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifacts; evaluating an LLM’s ability to transform multimodal instructions into high-quality, executable interactive visual artifacts across diverse prompts; providing a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: We release dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Automated filters drop incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items; flagged items are re-authored or discarded; experts rewrite prompts for clarity/completeness/executability, LLM rewriting adds diverse styles, humans verify; tasks solved only by brittle hacks are revised or removed; difficulty is assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models to enforce a 30%/40%/30% split, stable under leave-family-out resampling.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two-stage de-duplication and contamination control is applied: MinHash plus semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS, and screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts; automated filters also drop incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items.
